captions.instagram:
How does a fire extinguisher work?

A fire extinguisher is a steel bottle of gas pushing on an agent, and the agent only works because it removes one of the four things a fire needs. Pull the pin, learn why you aim at the base, and see why water on cooking oil makes a fireball.

→ A fire extinguisher is a steel bottle of agent with gas squeezed in above it.
→ Pull the pin, squeeze the lever, and the gas pushes the agent up a tube and out.
→ A fire needs fuel, oxygen, heat and a chain reaction. Take away any one and it dies.
→ P.A.S.S. Pull the pin. Aim low, at the base of the fire, where the fuel is.
→ Squeeze, and sweep side to side. Flames are only gas rising from fuel, so the base is what counts.

Play with it yourself. It's free and open source: glassbox.how/extinguisherclear (link in bio)

youtubeLong.title: How does a fire extinguisher work? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
A fire extinguisher is a steel bottle of gas pushing on an agent, and the agent only works because it removes one of the four things a fire needs. Pull the pin, learn why you aim at the base, and see why water on cooking oil makes a fireball.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox.how/e/extinguisherclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/extinguisherclear

In this video:
• A bottle of gas pushing on an agent. A stored-pressure extinguisher is a cylinder with the agent (water, foam or powder) at the bottom and nitrogen or dry air above it at about 12 to 15 bar.
• A fire needs four things. The fire triangle is fuel, oxygen and heat.
• PASS: aim at the base. Pull the pin, Aim at the base, Squeeze the lever, Sweep side to side.
• The wrong extinguisher makes it worse. Fires are sorted by fuel: A solids, B liquids, C gases, D metals, F cooking oil (K in the US).
• CO₂: a liquid that boils into snow. A CO₂ extinguisher holds liquid carbon dioxide at its own vapour pressure: about 57 bar at 20 °C and 35 bar at 0 °C.
• Ready when you need it. The gauge needle should sit in the green.
